legal.norm: Electoral Code (Dz.U.2026.1261 t.j.) art. 201: at least 7 deputies per constituency; art. 202: seats by a uniform norm of representation, residents divided by seats, fractions of 1/2 or more rounded up; art. 203: PKW proposes boundary changes when the territorial division or population changes.

caveats: Seats follow residents, not electors or voters: the Electoral Code (art. 201-203) gives every constituency at least 7 seats and sets the rest by a norm of representation, residents per seat, so electors per seat and votes per seat differ from it.
The 41 constituencies and their seat numbers (annex 1 to the Code) did not change between 2001 and 2023 except for a few seats; the population did, which is why the vote's value drifts.

Residents are GUS BDL's population on 31 December of the year before the election (2001: 31 December 2002, the first year of today's gmina structure), summed over today's gminas; they cover 99.6% of GUS's total in 2001-11 and 99.9% or more from 2015. Residents are not available on this basis for 1991-97.

Electors registered abroad or on ships are counted by PKW in the Warsaw constituency (19): 43,000 in 2001, 191,000 in 2007, 350,000 in 2019 and 637,000 in 2023. They are real voters for Warsaw's seats, so the headline measures count them; each measure is also shown without them (electors at home), and residents never include them. Most of the rise in the malapportionment of electors in 2023 is this: 4.0% with them, 2.7% without.

The vote value index is the national average of electors (or votes, or residents) per seat divided by the constituency's: above 1 means a vote counts for more. It is relative to the election's own national average, so it compares constituencies within an election; the malapportionment index (half the sum of the absolute differences between seat and elector shares) compares elections.

The 69 national-list seats of 1991-97 are not in the constituency measures; they are listed apart. The 1991 allocation (Hare-Niemeyer) cannot be reproduced from list votes alone, so 1991 has no last-seat measures.

The votes behind the last seat are the quotient of the last seat won (D'Hondt divisor or modified Sainte-Lague); a list needs more than 1 / (M + 1) of the votes of the lists in contention to be sure of a seat under D'Hondt. Lists below the national threshold (5%, 8% for a coalition) take no part; minority lists are exempt. Wasted votes are votes for lists that won no seat in the constituency.
Sieradz in 2007 does not reproduce from the votes in PKW's file (the last seat's quotient is 26,706 against 26,820 for the first lost); it is also Election results' one warning.
MPs are those who held a seat for the constituency in the term after the election, replacements included; there are no ranked lists.
